eli5.text: The project upgraded its core build tool to the newest stable version everywhere at once, keeping the engine requirement and the helper type packages in lockstep so they all ask for the same newer release instead of the older one. Anyone building or running the project locally will pull in the updated tool automatically and may see slightly faster startup and fewer install hiccups, while the bundled web editor interface also receives its newest set of ready-made UI pieces. No visible switches or new buttons appear; it is purely behind-the-scenes housekeeping that tightens the shared version numbers across every package and keeps the developer experience on the latest stable release.

ai.title: CLI skips agent registry init on --agent flag
ai.summary: cli/src/index.tsx conditionally skips initializeAgentRegistry() when --agent flag provides non-empty value, unless publish command detected. Reduces startup overhead for explicit agent overrides. Scope limited to CLI entrypoint.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant and tell it which helper to use by name, it no longer pauses to load the full list of helpers on your computer first. For example, if you run a command like 'help --agent my-special-helper', the assistant skips opening that list. If you don't name a specific helper, or if you are publishing something, the assistant still loads the full list as before. This makes starting up a bit faster when you are using the --agent option, and it only affects how the command line tool starts.

ai.summary: Added nightly-agents-e2e.yml to run .agents e2e tests daily at 12:00 UTC. CI workflow updated to skip .agents integration tests, requiring local execution via bun run test:e2e. sdk/e2e/utils/get-api-key.ts modified to require RUN_CODEBUFF_E2E=true for local live API runs unless running in CI. sdk/test/setup-env.ts removed default CODEBUFF_API_KEY to enforce explicit configuration.

eli5.text: Test runs that used to run during every code change now happen once a day in the background, so routine checks finish faster. The tests that need real online services no longer start up during work hours at all. If you run them yourself, you'll need to turn on a special setting before they will talk to the live system.

eli5.text: The company updated the tool they use to build and test their software, bumping it to a newer version across all their automated testing systems. This won't affect anything you do directly, but if you peek behind the scenes, you'd see the version number changed in four separate configuration files. Everything still works the same, it's just housekeeping to stay current with reliable versions.

ai.title: Document --agent override behavior
ai.summary: Clarified that `--agent` skips loading local `.agents` overrides to prevent unintended agent substitution. Updated `README.md`, `cli/src/index.tsx` help text, and `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/README.md` to reflect this behavior and correct testing instructions. Developers must now run `codebuff` without `--agent` to test local agent definitions.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant tool to run a specific helper program by name, it now skips any custom helper programs you may have saved in your project's folder. Previously, even when you named a specific helper, the tool would still load your project's own helper files, which could accidentally swap in a different helper than the one you wanted. Now those project helpers stay out of the way when you explicitly name a helper, so the one you pick is the one that runs. This only applies when you request a named helper from the command line; leaving that option off still loads your project's helpers as before.

ai.title: Freebuff 1.0.559 ships Bun 1.3.5 and CLI --agent skip
ai.summary: Version 1.0.559 packages the day's same-sequence work: a workspace-wide Bun upgrade to 1.3.5 across all package.json engines, devDependencies, and packageManager fields plus @opentui/core and @opentui/react bumped to ^0.1.63; the CLI entrypoint now skips initializeAgentRegistry() when a non-empty --agent flag is provided (excluding the publish command), reducing startup overhead for explicit agent overrides; and a nightly e2e workflow was added while CI now skips .agents integration tests, requiring local execution via `bun run test:e2e` and enforcing explicit RUN_CODEBUFF_E2E=true and CODEBUFF_API_KEY configuration. The version bump itself covers these user-facing CLI and toolchain improvements from 1.0.558.
ai.evidence: Diff shows only a single-line version increment in `cli/release/package.json`, bumping `codebuff` from `1.0.558` to `1.0.559`. No other files were modified in this commit, and the release updates list summarizes the prior same-day commits for Bun 1.3.5, CLI --agent flag init skip, and nightly e2e workflow additions.

eli5.text: Freebuff 1.0.559 brings faster, more reliable starts for developers who use the command-line tool with the --agent option, plus a major upgrade to the underlying Bun runtime that powers all the tools. When you run the CLI with a specific agent already selected, it now skips a background setup step that used to happen automatically, so you get to your work screen quicker instead of waiting for an agent list to load. The Bun engine, which runs the code behind the scenes, was upgraded from version 1.3.0 to 1.3.5 across the entire system, meaning everything from running commands to loading projects is now using the latest, most stable version, with improved speed and bug fixes. A new nightly testing routine was also set up to automatically check the agent features every day, while day-to-day CI builds will no longer run those slow live tests, keeping your regular updates faster to download and verify. Upgrading gives you these speed boosts, the stability of the latest Bun release, and clearer documentation on how the --agent flag works so you don't accidentally override your own custom agent settings.

eli5.text: The automated check that confirms agent edits are recorded now scans both the visible assistant output and a behind-the-scenes session log for proof of the edit, and it accepts a broader set of telltale phrases. This makes the check reliably pass in live internal testing starting today; if you run the editor-best-of-n scenario you'll get a stable pass instead of a flaky failure caused by missing evidence terms in the output alone.

ai.title: CLI project picker logic fix
ai.summary: New `shouldShowProjectPicker` helper in `cli/src/utils/project-picker.ts` replaces ad-hoc checks in `cli/src/index.tsx`. Previous logic incorrectly triggered the picker for valid non-git project directories. The new implementation uses `path.relative` to strictly limit the picker to the home directory or its ancestors. Covers CLI entry point and utilities.

eli5.text: When you open the terminal in your home directory or a folder nearby, the project picker now correctly appears to help you choose a project. Previously, it would sometimes pop up in folders where it wasn't needed. The fix replaces scattered checks with a single, clearer rule: show the picker only when your current folder is your home directory or an ancestor of it. You'd notice this if you regularly navigate from your home folder, the picker will appear when expected and stay hidden otherwise.

ai.title: Show git root notice in top banner
ai.summary: Added `gitRoot` type to `TopBannerType` and implemented a new top banner in `top-banner.tsx` that appears when the current working directory differs from the git root. The banner provides a `Switch to git root` action via `TerminalLink`. `init-app.ts` updated to set `projectRoot` to `baseCwd` instead of defaulting to `findGitRoot`, allowing the new logic to correctly detect subdirectory starts.

eli5.text: When you start the assistant inside a folder that sits inside a larger project (for example, a subfolder of your code repository), the program previously got confused about which directory was the main one. Now, when that situation is detected, a small notice appears at the top of your screen telling you that you are in a subfolder, along with a clickable link to switch over to the project's main folder. The switch also refreshes the project's location correctly, so your work stays connected to the right place.

ai.title: CLI build script uses production mode
ai.summary: The CLI binary build script in cli/scripts/build-binary.ts now passes --production to bun build. This ensures the compiled binary excludes development-only code and optimizations. Scope limited to CLI packaging.

eli5.text: The downloadable command-line tool now builds itself in its final, ready-to-run form instead of including extra helper code meant only for testing. Anyone who installs the standalone command-line tool will receive a smaller, cleaner version with development-only features stripped out. If you peek at the installation package, you won't find the debugging scripts or test-mode shortcuts that previously tagged along.

ai.title: Document --compile flag purpose in CLI binary build
ai.summary: Added comment to `--compile` flag in `cli/scripts/build-binary.ts`. Explains flag ensures compiled binaries use production JSX runtime to avoid `jsxDEV` crashes. Change affects CLI build script only. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: When the command-line tool is packaged into a standalone program for download, a behind-the-scenes note was added to make sure it always runs in its fast, production mode instead of the slower developer mode that can crash. This is purely a clarification for the people who build the program, so you won't notice anything different in the final app itself.

ai.title: Version bumped to 1.0.560
ai.summary: The codebuff package version in cli/release/package.json was incremented from 1.0.559 to 1.0.560 as part of the standard release cycle. This version bump captures several user-facing CLI improvements shipped since the prior release, including a fix to the project picker logic that previously triggered incorrectly for valid non-git directories, a new top banner notification when the working directory differs from the git root, and refinements to e2e test assertions for editor best-of-n flows. The build script also now invokes bun build with --production to exclude development-only code from compiled binaries.
ai.evidence: The diff in cli/release/package.json shows the version field bumped from 1.0.559 to 1.0.560 within the codebuff package manifest, reflecting a routine release increment with no functional code changes in this specific commit.

eli5.text: Version 1.0.560 makes the command-line tool smarter about where it works and clearer about where it is. The project picker no longer pops up incorrectly when you're working inside a normal project folder, so you can start coding without an extra selection step, and a new banner now appears at the top of your terminal whenever you're working inside a subfolder of a larger project, giving you a one-click option to jump back to the project's root folder. The built-in tests that check how the editing assistant proposes changes have been updated to be more reliable, so new features and fixes are less likely to break existing behavior. The final compiled program is now built using production settings behind the scenes, which keeps development-only code out of the downloadable tool you install, making it lighter and more stable when you're using it day to day.

ai.summary: CI setup action replaces hardcoded bun-version input with bun-version-file pointing to .bun-version. oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 now reads the version from the file instead of a literal string. eli5.text: The system that builds and tests our software used to have the version number typed directly into its setup instructions, so every time the version changed it had to be updated in multiple places. Now it reads the version from a single file that is already followed everywhere else the software is used, which means you won't see anything different today but you can be confident the testing side won't drift out of step with the version everyone agreed on. If you maintain that version file, everything else now stays in agreement automatically; if you don't, tests will keep working today but may point at a version that no longer exists once the file goes missing.

ai.evidence: Commit [7f288ce4] modifies `cli/release/package.json`, changing the version field from "1.0.560" to "1.0.561" (diff hunk: `- "version": "1.0.560",` / `+ "version": "1.0.561",`). No functional code files changed in this commit.

eli5.text: This release focuses on cleaning up the Freebuff CLI experience and making the build process clearer for development. It removes an old demo GIF from the README file and the assets folder, which shrinks the repository size. The production build flag comment has been repositioned next to the flag it describes, so anyone building the CLI understands why the production setting is needed to avoid crashes. The CI pipeline now automatically reads the Bun runtime version from a dedicated version file instead of hardcoding it, keeping builds in sync with local development. Overall, these changes improve documentation clarity, reduce clutter, and help developers who contribute to Freebuff get up and running faster.

ai.title: PostgreSQL transient errors now retry with jittered backoff
ai.summary: Database transactions retry on PostgreSQL transient failures (classes 08, 40, 53, 57) using expanded logic in packages/internal/src/db/transaction.ts. withRetry in common/src/util/promise.ts adds ±20% jitter to exponential backoff to prevent thundering herd. Billing balance-calculator.ts extracts pgCode, pgConstraint, and related fields into structured logs for debugging.

eli5.text: When the database temporarily stumbles under load, the system now waits a short, slightly random amount of time before trying again instead of all parts retrying at once. This makes the database less likely to get overwhelmed during busy periods. The retry now covers specific types of connection and timeout errors that used to stop operations mid-flight. If you run the software today, you would notice fewer failures when the database is under stress.

Additionally, the BigQuery mock setup is now included when running tests, making automated checks more consistent. These changes are maintenance work today; you won't see a new feature, but the tool's underlying setup is cleaner and its test suite is more reliable.
